s.answer:
Worked example: n8n against a HubSpot trial.

Webhook (form) → IF header x-form-secret = $env.FORM_SECRET
  → Execute Workflow 'Upsert enquiry'
Gmail Trigger (label portal) → Code parse → IF ok
  → Upsert enquiry (source_event_id = message id) : Telegram alert 'parse failed'
Upsert enquiry: seen event? stop → normalise → search email/phone
  → update (no blank overwrite) / create → deal → note → log

Test: same event ×3 → 1 deal, log shows created, skipped, skipped. Changed portal template → parse alert within 1 minute.
s.pass: An upsert sub-workflow plus a secured form webhook and an email parser; three identical events create one deal; the log records all three; a parse failure raises an alert.
s.redo: Send it back if duplicates appear on repeat events, the webhook accepts unsigned calls, or parse failures are silent.

g.answer:
Worked example of evidence: test-mode run.

Forged webhook (bad signature) ........ 401, deal unchanged ✓
Test payment KORA-812-1730 (₦50,000) .. verified via API ✓
  → deal 812 → Legal and payment (once) ✓ · accounts notified ✓
Replay of same webhook ................ skipped (event seen) ✓
WhatsApp template enquiry_received .... delivered to own phone ✓
Contact without WhatsApp consent ...... email sent instead ✓
mistakes: Matching payments by amount or name.
g.pass: A forged webhook is rejected, a real test-mode payment moves the right deal once after verification, a replay is skipped, and the WhatsApp acknowledgement arrives only for opted-in contacts.
g.redo: Send it back if the payment isn't verified with Paystack's API, matching isn't by your own reference, or consent isn't checked.
